title: Resolve Windows launcher shims to native executables; avoid shell spawning
context: On Windows, spawn("npx", ..., {shell: false}) fails because launchers like npx.cmd cannot be executed directly by Node. The error was swallowed silently, recording exit_code: null for every verify check, making cards show 'no independent command result' on Windows only. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Created resolveSpawnCommand() to map commands to their real executables before spawn: npm/npx run as Node CLI scripts (no shell, no shim), .cmd/.bat route through cmd.exe with shell:false + windowsVerbatimArguments and pre-quoted args, direct executables spawn as-is. Platform detection inlines the logic at spawn time.
consequences: Verification checks now record real exit codes on Windows instead of null
npm/npx avoid shell entirely by invoking the underlying CLI script
Batch launchers still use shell:false for security/perf, only cmd.exe hosts the args
Command resolution tracks how it was resolved (npm-cli, cmd-shim, pathext, direct) for debugging
Windows PATH and PATHEXT are traversed correctly, not bypassed by shell
alternatives_rejected: Use shell:true globally — simpler but loses security and performance of shell:false
Route all Windows commands through cmd.exe — unnecessary overhead for .exe files
Only support Windows in CI; skip local developer verification — doesn't fix the root problem
